fact: Never use expect_identical() on C++ double return values in cross-platform tests. Use expect_equal(tolerance = N * .Machine$double.eps) instead.
why: expect_identical() on doubles fails across platforms (macOS ARM64 vs Linux x86) by 1-3 ULP due to differing FMA vs non-FMA code generation. The algorithm is deterministic within a platform but not across platforms.

fact: For cross-platform tolerance on C++ ensemble bootstrap tests, use tolerance = n_boot * .Machine$double.eps, not a fixed small constant like 8 * .Machine$double.eps.
why: Each of n_boot bootstrap replicates accumulates one FP rounding step. With n_boot=500 the bound is ~1.1e-13; using 8*eps (~1.8e-15) fails on macOS where FP code generation differs.

fact: expect_equal(x, y, tolerance=t) uses relative comparison by default. When both values are near 0, add scale=1 to switch to absolute comparison.
why: Relative tolerance divides by |target|; when target ≈ 0 the ratio explodes. A diff of 2e-16 failed with tolerance=1e-14 on robLoc output near 0 (n=32, symmetric normal sample).

fact: Add devtools to Suggests in DESCRIPTION if any test file calls devtools::load_all(), even inside tryCatch().
why: R CMD check flags any package called in tests that is not in Depends/Imports/Suggests as an unstated dependency WARNING, regardless of whether the call is guarded.

fact: NEVER extrapolate serial memory cost from a single-pass benchmark when the function uses Aitken/Steffensen multi-pass iteration. rob_scale_compute calls rho_sum ~10 times per outer iteration; serial traffic at n=32768 is ~2.6MB, not n/8192 * single-pass cost.
why: Raised rob_scale_parallel_threshold from 16384 to 65536 based on linear extrapolation of n=8192 serial cost; caused 33% regression at n=32768 (852µs serial >> 639µs parallel). Real serial cost grows ~10x faster than single-pass extrapolation suggests.

fact: Sub-µs micro-benchmarks cannot determine algorithm crossover points on this machine (timer quantum ~419-489ns). When both implementations complete in <4 quanta (~2µs), reported crossover bounces across 3 runs (e.g. n=10, n=32, n=32). Fall back to theoretical analysis.
why: WU-RS3 threshold benchmark at n=8..32 showed all times clustering at 4-5 timer quanta; 'crossover' was inconsistent across 3 identical runs. Empirical data was pure quantization noise.

fact: SOLO gate baselines captured at sub-µs sizes contain quantization noise at capture time. A ratio >1.05 against a SOLO baseline at n<=65 may be ONE timer quantum of noise, not a real regression. Apply 3-run consensus: require failure in all 3 runs before acting.
why: n=16 (ratio=1.23) and n=65 (ratio=1.15) both failed in run 1 but passed in runs 2-3. Each difference was exactly ~419-489ns (1 timer quantum). The baseline captured a randomly-quantized value.

fact: covr::package_coverage() on this system (GCC -flto=auto --coverage) strips Rcpp .Call() exports from the .so — symbols only referenced via R's .Call() at runtime are invisible to the LTO linker. Affected: C_sn_sorted, C_qn_sorted (ensemble.cpp). CI uses R CMD check only, so this silent breakage never surfaces in CI.
why: 87 tests fail with 'not an exported object from namespace:robscale' in covr build; same tests pass in devtools::test(). Normal build nm shows the symbols; covr build .so does not. Pre-existing issue, not introduced by optimization work.

fact: rob_scale_gate_check.R sizes vector includes n=7 but the SOLO baseline was captured without it. The 'no baseline' fallback returns list(n=n, ratio=NA, pass=TRUE) missing 'sub_us', causing crash when printing. Run SOLO mode only for sizes present in the baseline.
why: Running 'Rscript bench/rob_scale_gate_check.R SOLO' crashes at n=7 with 'argument is of length zero'. The gate script sizes and baseline were created in separate sessions with different size vectors.

fact: When WUs have uncommitted changes, git diff HEAD --name-only shows ALL working-tree modifications across ALL parallel WUs — adversarial reviewers will report false scope-violation FAILs for files belonging to other WUs. Commit each WU before spawning its reviewer, or instruct the reviewer to check git diff HEAD -- <declared-files> to isolate only the reviewed WU's changes.
why: Parallel WU execution leaves multiple WUs' changes uncommitted simultaneously. git diff HEAD --name-only is a flat listing of all dirty files, not a per-WU view. Reviewers mistakenly flag files from sibling WUs as out-of-scope violations.

fact: When extracting a C++ hot inner-loop template into a shared helper with multiple call sites, static inline alone is insufficient at -O2 — GCC/Clang may refuse to inline across call sites, causing ~5x regression. Use __attribute__((always_inline)) static inline to guarantee inlining.
why: WU-CLEAN-3 extracted sn_inner_serial from three call sites in sn_estimator.cpp. static inline showed ~5x regression at n=1000; adding __attribute__((always_inline)) recovered the performance. The compiler will not always honour inline at -O2 when the same function body is called from multiple sites.

fact: Running bench gate scripts without arguments silently re-captures a new baseline instead of verifying the current code. Always run 'Rscript bench/<gate>.R CHECK' during final comprehensive review to compare against the pre-change baseline.
why: Gate scripts default to CAPTURE mode (no args = save baseline). Running them without CHECK in the final review creates a new baseline from the post-change code, making the gate trivially pass and destroying the pre-change reference point.

fact: Fixing boot::boot inner parallelism (switching to parallel='no') without capping the outer mclapply still over-commits: detectCores(logical=FALSE) workers × ~1GB each can exceed available RAM on a machine already under swap pressure, causing an OOM crash. The outer fork count must also be bounded.
why: analyze_results.R was fixed to run boot::boot serially inside mclapply workers (preventing n_cores^2 forks). But mclapply still used all 16 physical cores. With 9+ GB swap already in use, 16 workers × ~800MB = crash. The inner fix was necessary but not sufficient.

fact: Running tar_invalidate() on a downstream target while src_files/r_files are already stale (e.g. after R CMD INSTALL) triggers a full pipeline rerun — not just the invalidated target. targets cascades from the stale file-hash targets through legacy_bench → rob_optimized → analyzed_results. Run tar_outdated() first to understand actual rerun scope before calling tar_invalidate().
why: tar_invalidate('speedup_figure_obj') was called after a package recompile. Because src_files was stale, targets reran the entire benchmark pipeline (~2h) instead of just the figure targets.

fact: NEVER add Aitken/Steffensen acceleration to rob_loc_compute or rob_loc_parallel_compute. robLoc uses quadratic NR (observed Hessian: sum_dpsi = Σ sech²((x_i−t)/(2s))), not linear IRLS (fixed expected-info denominator). Empirical: n=100 normal — plain NR 3 evals, Aitken 3 evals (tie); contaminated data — Aitken 4 evals (+1, worse).
why: Aitken targets linear iterations where |T'(t*)| < 1 with T'(t*)≠0. For quadratic NR, T'(t*)=0 and convergence takes 2-3 steps. Aitken's minimum cost (2 evals per outer step) equals the full baseline, so no savings are possible. The plan assumed T'(t*)≈−0.57 (IRLS), which is wrong for this implementation.

fact: Place shared C++ template helpers BEFORE any #ifdef conditional block that uses them, even when the condition is off for the current build. The compiler's front-end parses all branches; a forward reference inside #ifdef is still a forward reference — the compiler reports 'not declared in this scope' when the condition is enabled.
why: aitken_loc_iterate was inserted after the TBB #ifdef block. rob_loc_parallel_compute (inside the block) could not see it; compile failed with 'aitken_loc_iterate was not declared in this scope' even though TBB was enabled. Inserting the template before the block fixed it.

fact: In sequential pin tests iterating over multiple n values (n=4, n=5, n=6,...), each rnorm(n) call consumes exactly n draws in order. Any diagnostic script that skips or reorders an n value shifts every subsequent sequence, producing wrong reference values and 100+ spurious failures that look like algorithm divergence.
why: test-robScale.R iterates n=4 first; an exploration script starting at n=5 consumed 5 draws where the test consumed 4, shifting all later sequences by 1 draw. 100 failures appeared but only 2 real pin values had changed.

fact: rob_scale_gate_check.R defaults to H2H mode, which requires the C_rob_scale_orig diagnostic export. After removing the diagnostic export, always run 'Rscript bench/rob_scale_gate_check.R SOLO'; the default crashes with 'object C_rob_scale_orig not found'.
why: WU-PROD-4 removed the NR diagnostic exports (C_rob_scale_nr_impl, C_rob_scale_orig). Running the gate without SOLO immediately crashes. SOLO mode compares against the pre-captured baseline RDS rather than a live diagnostic function.

fact: When bench::mark() benchmarks two expressions, bm$median is a 2-element bench_time vector. Using as.numeric(bm$median) writes 2 values into the baseline RDS; gate scripts expecting scalar median_ns then crash on length checks. Always use bm$median[[1]] for scalar extraction in single-expression baselines.
why: The NR baseline script timed robScale(x) alongside C_rob_scale_orig(x) in one bench::mark() call. as.numeric(bm$median) silently produced a 2-element vector instead of a scalar, corrupting the baseline format.

fact: NR handles any positive s_init correctly because the scale is relative (hisc = hisc_pre / s). ADM does NOT downweight outliers — redirecting to ADM when MAD is small due to outliers (not near-constant data) gives WRONG results. The implosion guard gap (0 < s_init <= IMPLOSION_BOUND with fallback=0) is intentional, not a bug.
why: Adversarial review B2 claimed this was BLOCKING. Verification with c(1e-4, 0, 0, 4) showed NR gives correct M-scale ~1e-4 reflecting the bulk, while ADM gives ~1.25 including the outlier. The existing code was correct.

fact: R's any(!is.finite(x)) allocates a length-n logical vector on the heap on every call. At n=1000 this costs ~3.9µs + 7.9KB — 40-69% of sd_c4's total call time. Replace with a C++ find_first_nonfinite scan: zero allocation, short-circuits on first bad value.
why: A/B profiling showed R-side validation was the dominant overhead for all estimators except qn. sd_c4: 69% overhead. robScale: 55%. adm: 65% at n=50000. Moving to C++ validate_finite eliminated this entirely.

fact: Rcpp::RNGScope is constructed on every [[Rcpp::export]] by default, calling GetRNGstate/PutRNGstate (reads/writes R's 626-byte global RNG state). For pure-numeric estimators that never call R's RNG, add // [[Rcpp::export(rng = false)]] to eliminate this constant overhead.
why: sd_c4(rnorm(5)) dropped from 2.37µs to 1.89µs (20% faster) after adding rng=false. All 26 estimator exports had unnecessary RNGScope; only 3 ensemble CI functions actually use R::qnorm/R::pnorm.

fact: Two agents running R CMD INSTALL --preclean simultaneously on the same worktree create a stale 00LOCK-* file that blocks both. One agent's git stash corrupts the other's working state. Never parallelize agents that both need to compile and install the same R package.
why: WU-OPT-4 and WU-OPT-5 dispatched in parallel both hit 'failed to lock directory' errors. WU-OPT-5's git stash caused linker errors in WU-OPT-4. Had to stop WU-OPT-5 and finish sequentially.

fact: compute_all_estimators stores results[0]=sd_c4, results[1]=gmd, but the API maps estimator_id 0=gmd, 1=sd_c4. The BCa jackknife used res[estimator_id] directly at TWO sites (cpp_single_estimator_ci_bounds:411 AND cpp_scale_ensemble:598/603). Both need kEstIdToAllIdx remapping. Only indices 0 and 1 are swapped; 2-6 are identity.
why: Every BCa CI for gmd and sd_c4 was wrong — the jackknife acceleration was computed from the wrong estimator's leave-one-out values. The second call site (ensemble path) was caught by the iteration-3 Feasibility reviewer, not the original review.

fact: Interleaving !std::isfinite checks per element in a copy loop prevents autovectorization. The compiler cannot use memcpy/SIMD because the branch creates a control-flow dependency. Fix: validate at the boundary once with a separate scan, then use clean std::memcpy.
why: qn/sn copy loops checked isfinite per element. After moving validation to the C_qn_impl/C_sn_impl boundary and replacing with memcpy, the copy became autovectorizable.

fact: R::qnorm, R::pnorm, R::qchisq, and all R distribution quantile/CDF functions are deterministic — they do NOT read or write R's RNG state. Rcpp exports that call only these functions can safely use [[Rcpp::export(rng = false)]]. Only R::rnorm, R::runif, R::rbinom etc. (random GENERATION functions) require RNGScope.
why: The 3 ensemble CI exports retained RNGScope because they call R::qnorm/R::pnorm. Adding rng=false eliminated ~5KB memcpy (GetRNGstate/PutRNGstate) per call with zero correctness impact. Package now has 0 RNGScope instances.

fact: Audit parameter usage across ALL code paths, not just the hot path. Multi-parameter function signatures can hide dead buffers: rob_scale_core took (w, dev) but dev was only used on a triple-nested fallback path (has_loc && n<3 && s_init<=implbound). 50% of every arena allocation (16KB on large-n stack path) was dead weight on the 99.9% hot NR path.
why: The dev buffer existed because the original code needed scratch for adaptive_mad_select. After NR was fused (OPT-F), dev became dead on the hot path but remained in the signature. Replacing with a 4-element local buffer on the rare fallback halved arena sizes.

fact: Never call RuntimeConfig::get() (TLS lookup) inside a function that runs per-bootstrap-replicate. With n_boot=1000, that is 1000 unnecessary TLS reads. Add a bool use_avx2 parameter to any function called in hot loops; hoist the TLS read to the loop boundary (once per thread in TBB lambda, once before serial loop).
why: gmd_weighted_sum called RuntimeConfig::get() internally. In the ensemble bootstrap, this meant 1000 TLS lookups per scale_robust() call. Adding use_avx2=false default parameter kept non-hot callers working while eliminating the hot-loop overhead.

fact: When hoisting a TLS read from a callee into a caller, the caller's #if guard must be at least as BROAD as the callee's. rob_loc_core's TBB block used #if TBB && AVX2, but rob_loc_compute used #if AVX2 alone. Hoisting from inside the TBB block leaves the flag undefined on non-TBB AVX2 builds. The hoist must use the callee's guard (#if AVX2), not the caller's narrower guard.
why: The plan review gate caught this: passing use_avx2 from rob_loc_core's #if TBB block would fail on non-TBB AVX2 builds where rob_loc_compute still needs the flag. Fixed by hoisting unconditionally with #if AVX2 before the #if TBB block.
